title: Rural Home Loans Annual Escrow Analysis: Deposit, Shortage and Surplus
content:
Escrow administration policy for the analysis of a Rural Home Loans escrow account.

## Clauses in force

1. Escrow is analysed once a year in the month of the closing anniversary, and at the end of a forbearance plan.
2. The base deposit is one-twelfth of that total rounded up to the cent.
3. When the projected low point (the lowest month-end escrow balance projected from the current escrow balance, the current monthly escrow deposits and the projected disbursements in their due months) is below the cushion, the difference is a shortage: it is added to the base deposit in equal parts over the product's shortage spread months, unless the member pays it at once as a lump-sum shortage deposit, in which case the deposit is the base deposit alone.
4. When the projected low point exceeds the cushion, the difference is a surplus: a surplus of at least the product's surplus refund minimum is refunded within the product's surplus refund days of the analysis when no monthly payment is past due; a smaller surplus, or any surplus while a payment is past due, stays in escrow and lowers the projection.
5. A loan with escrow waived has no analysis.
6. At payoff, any escrow balance is refunded within the product's surplus refund days.

## Retired clauses

- **Retired clause — no longer in force; superseded by the current basis.** "The analysis projects the next 12 months of disbursements (the property tax installments, insurance premiums and mortgage insurance premiums expected to be paid from escrow in the 12 months following the analysis date, each at the amount of the latest bill of the same kind)"
- **Retired clause — no longer in force; superseded by the current basis.** "and the account may keep a cushion of the product's cushion months twelfths of the total above zero at its projected low point"

## Shortage and surplus as definitions

- The shortage is the cushion less the projected low point, and nothing when that is below zero.
- The surplus is the projected low point less the cushion, and nothing when that is below zero.
- The new monthly escrow deposit is the base deposit plus the shortage divided by the shortage spread months, rounded to the cent; with the shortage paid at once as a lump-sum deposit, it is the base deposit alone.

## Surplus points of judgement

| Surplus found | Any monthly payment past due | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| at or above the refund minimum | no | refunded within the refund days |
| at or above the refund minimum | yes | stays in escrow and lowers the projection |
| below the refund minimum | either | stays in escrow and lowers the projection |

A monthly payment is past due when its bill's due date is earlier than the day considered and the amount paid on it is below the monthly principal-and-interest payment, forborne months excluded.

superseded_clauses: The analysis projects the next 12 months of disbursements (homeloan_msr_projected_disbursements)
and the account may keep a cushion of escrow_cushion_months twelfths of the total above zero at its projected low point
